newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Costello talks of his vision.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Costello talks of his vision.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello, seen as a possible successor to Prime Minister John Howard, spoke on Friday of "my vision" for the nation.
Costello outlined his seven-point vision for Australia at a conference convened to debate the future of Victoria state, the nation's traditional industrial heartland, in the year 2010.
"Let me tell you the elements of my vision for the year 2010," Costello began.

He said wanted to see a cohesive nation "at ease with itself and its institutions", boasting the world's best natural environment, able to care for its elderly and fiscally responsible to future generations.
His vision also included a society full of opportunities for its youth and a nation that was a leader in the Asia-Pacific.
Costello's remarks about Australia being a regional leader "at ease" with itself were similar to those once made by a predecessor as treasurer, former prime minister Paul Keating.

Howard's Liberal-National administration won a landslide election victory in March and electoral analysts say the Labor opposition, well behind in opinion polls, is unlikely to win the next election, due in early 1999.

Government members of parliament say Costello and Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith are the obvious candidates to eventually replace Howard, although none speculates that the prime minister will leave office anytime soon.
